reason: Each case needs a credentialed agent runtime to produce the answer under test, and no such runtime ships with this payload, so these cases are recorded acceptance criteria rather than a runnable suite. The skill's knowledge claims are checked deterministically in the adopting repo's own tests.

cases.prompt: Our deploy gate has been red since March. Everyone treats it as known noise, so can we just lower its threshold and move on?

assertions.value: refuses to tune a check that has never been observed green, and proposes running it against an explicit healthy subject and an explicit defective one before any decision

cases.prompt: My verifier prints UNVERIFIABLE when it cannot read the running image, and the CI step fails on that line. Is that the right behaviour?

assertions.value: separates not-evaluated from violated, requires the missing input to be detected explicitly, and requires that no retry, re-send or delete follows a not-evaluated verdict

cases.prompt: The check passes on my machine and fails in CI, and the image ids look identical to me. What should I look at first?

assertions.value: attributes the mismatch to representation first, and requires both sides to be passed through one normalising function before their equality is trusted

cases.prompt: Our guard has refused on every run since a restart script renamed the target window. Should I add the new name to the accepted list?

assertions.value: asks whether the guarded action still needs the guard at all before widening it, and if an exception is kept, requires it to be declared data that is itself checked
